title: evals action-queue scratchpad (weekly prep)
body:
Purpose / constraints: quick 30min weekly triage with Rhea and Maya — focus on the three worst regressions from last 48h, decide immediate mitigations, and pin owners for longer-term fixes. Keep decisions timeboxed (max 10m per regression). This is a scratchpad; messy.

Meeting agenda (30m total):
- 0-5m: quick metrics snapshot + any infra incidents that could explain noise
- 5-15m: regression A deep-dive (owner: Rhea)
- 15-25m: regression B + C quick triage (owners: Maya / Oliver)
- 25-30m: commit owners + deadlines + follow-ups, sanity check on ongoing ABs

Pre-reads (one-line):
- AB experiment #314: baseline vs prompt-v2 (link in linked_artifacts) — signal tilt in generation length
- Eval run 2026-03-08: summary CSV attached to GH PR
- infra-gpu-sched active alerts: none in last 24h (checked at 09:10PT)

Metrics snapshot (pull from quick sql tomorrow morning):
- avg latency (p50/p95): 112ms / 310ms (hosted-api-us-west)
- token cost delta vs last week: +4.2% (likely due to longer generations in A-arm)
- user-visible failure rate: 0.45% (up from 0.12%)

Top regressions observed (quick notes + hypotheses + immediate action):
1) Regression A: "hallucination spike" on knowledge questions (finance domain)
   - signal: +18% hallucination rate on curated finance prompts (eval-suite v12)
   - recent change: prompt templating tweak merged in PR GH:redwood/evals#412 (prompt-v2)
   - hypothesis: new stop-token placement encourages longer completions that veer off-topic
   - immediate mitigation: rollback to prompt-v1 for traffic slice (canary) OR add stricter few-shot anchors; decision: start canary rollback for 10% traffic (owner: Rhea).
   - follow-up: Rhea to open rollback PR + add 6 curated seeds to check for anchoring effect (due: 2026-03-12).

2) Regression B: "short-answer truncation" in summarization microtask
   - signal: short summaries truncated mid-sentence for inputs > 800 tokens (eval-run shows abrupt stop)
   - recent change: token-budget clamp introduced in runtime (commit abc123) to limit tail latency
   - hypothesis: clamp is too aggressive for >800 tokens inputs; truncation threshold off-by-one in budget calc
   - immediate mitigation: relax clamp by +10% for dedicated summarization route; owner: Maya to patch routing config.
   - follow-up: Maya to add targeted unit test and run local sim with long inputs (due: 2026-03-14).

3) Regression C: "A/B drift" — A-arm yields higher lexical diversity but lower factuality on entity-heavy prompts
   - signal: A-arm (prompt-v2) higher self-contradiction measure, p=0.03 significance vs baseline
   - hypothesis: the extra context tokens in prompt-v2 bias generative sampling toward paraphrase rather than canonical facts
   - immediate mitigation: pause expansion of prompt context for domain-specific routes; owner: Oliver to gate expansion in routing rules.
   - follow-up: Oliver to run comparison with temperature fixed at 0.0 and 0.2 to see interaction (due: 2026-03-13).

Prompt set housekeeping notes (candidates to drop / keep):
- keep prompt-v1 for finance and legal verticals until regression closed
- spin out a "short-summarizer" prompt set that forces sentence-boundary anchors for >800 token inputs
- candidate prompt to trial: prompt-v2a (stricter anchor examples + lower temperature suggestion) — run against sampled production traces (owner: Rhea).

A/B experiments to monitor:
- AB#314 (prompt-v2 vs baseline): currently 60/40 split, early signs of increased length + cost. Action: limit to 30/70 until hallucination rollback decisions resolved. (owner: Oliver)
- AB#321 (quantization-change on dedicated): no signal yet, but watch p95 latency for token spikes. (observer: infra)

Open questions / things to probe during meeting:
- Is the hallucination metric calibrated across full prompt suite? Do we need new labelers for finance prompts?
- Could recent model refresh (model-b-2026-03) interact with prompt changes? Cross-check with model-owner.
- Do any of the regressions map to a customer SLA incident (CS ticket backlog)? Quick cross-check with CS.

Concrete follow-ups & owners (post-meeting commitments):
- Rhea: initiate 10% prompt-v1 rollback + run 6 anchor seeds (due 2026-03-12)
- Maya: relax clamp for summarization route + add unit test (due 2026-03-14)
- Oliver: gate prompt expansion in routing rules and run temp sensitivity sims (due 2026-03-13)
- All: sync notes into GH issue and tag OPT-998 (owner: Oliver to create issue, due 2026-03-11)

Quick TODO checklist (my brain dump):
- [ ] collect per-prompt hallucination examples (2 each) -> to include in GH issue
- [ ] confirm rollback playbook with release-eng (who's oncall?)
- [ ] add AB#314 throttling in console to 30/70
- [ ] message CS with heads-up for finance customers (templated note)

Notes-to-self / private hunches (untested):
- We might be compounding two independent effects: longer outputs (cost) and more permissive anchors (quality). Fixing either might partially mask the other. Track both.
- If rollback doesn't fix hallucinations, escalate to model-owner for evaluation sweep across model-b-2026-03 artifacts.

End-of-scratchpad. Keep this short for meeting; move final decisions to GH issue after sync.

Small reminders: bring up 'safety labeler capacity' — we only have 12 labelers for finance vertical this sprint; may need to prioritize sampling.

(Last quick edit: 2026-03-10 09:25 PT)
